Study Layout

Experience

Lesson Goal

Practice a real snack bar shift in simple English. Welcome a foreign customer, explain the seat charge, ask about drinks, use safe small talk, offer karaoke without pressure, and say goodbye warmly.

Introduction

This lesson is for a snack bar worker or host. The English is mostly A1 to A2.

You do not need perfect English. You need short, warm, useful English for one real shift.

Key Idea

In Japan, a snack bar is a small local drinking place. Customers drink, talk with staff, relax, and sometimes do karaoke.

In English, snack bar can sound like a place for food and soft drinks, so foreign customers may need a simple explanation.

Main Question

Use the support language button at the top of the site when you want translations for hard words. The main practice stays in English, so the worker can get used to real workplace speech.

Warm-Up Questions

  • What do you say when a customer comes in?
  • What is hard to explain about your snack bar?
  • What drink words do you use at work?
  • What sentence do you want to say smoothly?

CLOSING

Good English is short, and clear. First, welcome the customer. Next, explain the place and the Then ask about After that, use small talk and make Finally, say and help the customer go home safely.

Final Reflection

Good snack bar English is warm, short, and clear. First, welcome the customer.

Next, explain the place and the seat charge. Then ask about drinks.

After that, use safe small talk and make karaoke optional. Finally, say goodbye warmly and help the customer go home safely.

Final Speaking Task
